abstract: Census Bureau Business Trends and Outlook Survey, biweekly cycle 202619 (reference period August 24 to September 6, 2026; collected September 7 to 20; published September 24, 2026). Question 7 asks whether a business used artificial intelligence in any of its business functions in the last two weeks; Question 24 asks whether it expects to within six months. National AI use reached 23.8 percent of firms, a fourth consecutive cycle-over-cycle increase and the highest reading in the series. This is the firm-side adoption series jobsdata.ai charts on ai-adoption-rate, dated to reference-period end rather than publication date.
keyFindings: 23.8 percent of US employer businesses used AI in the two weeks ending 2026-09-06 (cycle 202619, standard error 0.26 percentage points), up from 23.2 percent in cycle 202618 (ending 2026-08-23), 22.4 percent in 202617 (ending 2026-08-09) and 21.8 percent in 202616 (ending 2026-07-26).
27.6 percent expect to use AI in the next six months (Q24, SE 0.29 points), up from 27.3 percent in the prior cycle.
The gap between expected and current use narrowed slightly to 3.8 points from 4.1 points, as current use rose faster than expectations this cycle.
Current use has risen 2.3 points over the four cycles since the reference period ending 2026-07-12 (21.5 percent).
methodology: Biweekly survey of US nonfarm employer businesses with receipts of $1,000 or more, run by the Census Bureau from a sample of about 1.2 million businesses split into six panels, each asked to report once every 12 weeks. Published as experimental data. Cycle 202619 covered a two-week reference period (2026-08-24 to 2026-09-06), was collected 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-20 and published 2026-09-24. Figures are national response estimates from National.xlsx. The November 2025 rewording from AI use 'in producing goods or services' to 'in any business function' is a same-construct instrument change; Census publishes one continuous series and so does jobsdata.ai.
qualifiers: Tier 1: federal statistical survey. It is a firm-level share with a low per-firm bar (any AI use in any function in two weeks), not a measure of how much work AI performs. It cannot be compared directly with posting-based measures (about 5.9 percent of eligible hiring firms) or with vendor-payment measures such as Ramp's (about 44 percent of Ramp customers pay Anthropic). Response is voluntary. A Federal Register notice of 2026-09-09 proposes three new core AI follow-up questions asked only of AI-using firms; Q7 wording is not changed, but watch for a response-burden effect on Q7 once the new items field. The biannual AI Supplement is a separate instrument and should not be treated as the latest point in this series.
